sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Mg–Sn binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset MgSn-04Fri.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L → (Mg) + Mg2Sn, lies at 563.4 °C.
The Mg–Sn system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as congruent compound.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry (Hallstedt, 2025), which reproduces the assessment of S.G. Fries, unpublished work, 2004.
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
The melting point of Sn reproduced by the dataset is 231.9 °C.
The dataset places a eutectic (L → (Mg) + Mg2Sn) at 563.4 °C; the composition of L is x(Sn) = 0.110.
We obtain 204.0 °C for the eutectic reaction (L → Mg2Sn + (Sn)), where L has a mole fraction of 0.911.
Mg2Sn melts congruently at 775.5 °C and x(Sn) = 0.333.
At 1150 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −14298 J/mol, at x(Sn) = 0.380.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of Mg2Sn at 298.15 K is −25.64 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
